layer_boundary: Complex-level receptor configuration to STAT3; does not add LR binding evidence.
Alternative OSMR-containing CNTFR complex is kept distinct from LIFR-containing complex.
Cx43/coupling is a cellular output and is not encoded as a direct receptor-protein interaction.
Astrocyte FGF2 release and neuronal support are functional outputs; receptor subunit usage remains unresolved.
Synthetic type-III receptor experiments support receptor-associated kinase participation but are not native astrocyte or SCI evidence.
IRF/ISG induction is retained as a pathway-level output; no single kinase necessity is inferred.
HSV-1 restriction is a cellular function and is not encoded as direct IFNLR1-to-STAT1 binding.
TRAF2 recruitment is a receptor-proximal molecular interaction; it is distinct from downstream NF-kappaB output.
TNFR2-TRAF2 to NF-kappaB/JNK is a receptor-proximal pathway relay.
Alternative NF-kappaB/p100 processing is retained as a branch output and is ligand-form dependent.
Locomotor recovery after SCI is a functional output; no astrocyte-specific molecular edge is inferred.
Astrocyte CXCL12 induction and OPC repair are functional CNS outputs, not direct TNFR2-to-CXCL12 molecular binding.
IL1R2-IL1RAP decoy-complex assembly is retained as a receptor-complex boundary, not as an intracellular signaling edge.
IL1R2-mediated ligand sequestration and shedding are inhibitory functional outputs distinct from IL1R1-MyD88 relay steps.
The SCI astrocyte edge is IL1R1-based; it is not used to infer IL1R2 function.
CCR4 arrestin-biased signaling is retained as a GPCR branch in a matched receptor assay.
CCR7 G-protein and arrestin coupling are kept as parallel receptor-proximal outputs.
CXCR3A G-protein coupling is separated from CXCR3B splice-variant behavior.
CXCR3B beta-arrestin/ERK behavior is a splice-variant branch and not a general ligand-bias claim.
TGFBR-TRAF6 association is direct receptor-proximal evidence, separate from JNK/p38 output.
TRAF6-TAK1-to-JNK/p38 is retained at pathway-complex resolution.
BMPR2-LIMK1 is a noncanonical receptor-tail branch, distinct from SMAD1/5/9.
BMP-SMAD activation in spinal astrocytes is receptor/pathway evidence, not an inferred direct protein interaction.
CSPG induction is a cellular/extracellular functional output.
Astrocyte neurocan/scar formation is a functional output and remains CNS-injury comparator evidence.
PDGFR-Src receptor-associated activation is retained at receptor-proximal pathway resolution; the source does not establish a direct physical PDGFR-SRC interaction.
PDGFR-to-ERK is a receptor-proximal kinase branch with adaptor/redox context.
OPC migration is a cellular function supported by ERK perturbation.
FGF2-RhoA-YAP astrocyte proliferation is a functional/pathway output; FGFR identity is unresolved.
WNT5A-ROR2-JNK is retained as a noncanonical pathway complex; no direct binding edge is inferred.
Inflammatory spinal-neuron death is a functional output of the WNT-ROR2 pathway.
WNT5A-JNK neural differentiation and SCI repair are functional outputs with unresolved receptor identity.
Jagged1-Notch1 to STAT3 is a CNS astrocyte pathway branch, not a generic Notch output.
EDNRB/ETBR transcription is a downstream branch output.
HES5 induction is a transcriptional pathway output in injured spinal cord.
Astrogliosis and functional recovery are cellular/organismal outputs, not direct NICD interactions.
DLL4-versus-DLL1 signaling strength is retained as ligand-context-dependent Notch output; Module 20A LR ledgers remain untouched.
CNTFR-alpha astrocyte localization and functional receptor-complex competence are receptor-context evidence, not a direct claim about the unresolved LIFR-versus-OSMR branch in contusive SCI.
FGFR2-associated PI3K-AKT signaling is retained as a receptor-proximal SCI branch with a neuronal/microglial receiver boundary.
PDGFR-beta pathway inhibition changes fibrotic scar and recovery outputs after SCI; no direct ligand-receptor interaction is inferred.
VEGF-to-EGFR transactivation is retained as the tested branch; VEGFR paralog identity is unresolved.
Spinal neural stem-cell activation is a cellular output of the VEGF-EGFR transactivation branch.
Astrocytic RYK control of scar-border formation and wound healing is a SCI functional edge; the noncanonical PCP interpretation remains untested.
DLL4-NOTCH1/NICD control of IL-6 transcription is a reactive-astrocyte pathway edge, not a contusive-SCI Notch paralog claim.
IL-6-dependent STAT3 phosphorylation and astrocyte reactivity are downstream outputs of the DLL4-NOTCH1 branch.
TNFR2 agonist and PI3K-gamma inhibitor evidence support a receptor-proximal pathway branch but do not establish a direct TNFR2-PI3Kgamma physical interaction.
CSF1 source and astrocyte-targeted loss connect lesion-border astrocytes to microglial proliferation and repair outputs; no direct CSF1-CSF1R binding claim is inferred.
Astrocyte-specific IFNAR1 loss links IFN-beta response to repair outputs; direct IFNAR-JAK/STAT molecular ordering remains unresolved.
